- The trials folder has all 72 trials, 3 per cell for each of the 4 configs and 6 tasks. Each trial has a grade, a metrics and a result file. All 72 transcripts were found, they are all different files, and they all come from workflow `wf_1a6926f8-f6c`. No trial was INCOMPLETE.

The figure of 3.60 credits is an estimate, not the real spend. Round 2 should run that check before writing any result.

## Requirements without a real test

- R1 asks for "the requested circuit". No mock task checks the circuit itself. T1, T2 and T5 check only the alias, the shots, the number of measured qubits and that the counts match. `garnet:mock` returned random counts. `sirius:mock` returned `{"000": 200}` in all 12 T2 trials. A wrong circuit would pass. The MOVE-aware compile on T2 was never checked. Round 2 should parse the payload from `/api/v1/jobs/{id}/payload` and check the gate sequence. For example, T2 should contain MOVE gates through `COMPR1`.
- The pass rule in T1 says "1 job". `grade.py` grades only the last job and never counts the jobs. In 9 of the 12 T6 trials the agent sent a second job, and in 7 of the 9 mock T6 cases this was not flagged. Round 2 should make the job count a code check and decide whether a mock trial run before a real job is allowed.
- R2 is loose on bit order. `counts_match` in `/Users/claytonchancey/Desktop/quantum/spe/evals/graders/grade.py` also accepts the counts with every bitstring reversed. In r01-A-T1-1 the agent swapped `01` and `10` relative to the API, and the trial passed. Round 2 should either require the API's bit order or state this tolerance in R2.
- R5 is checked by regex only. `names_gate_fix` passes if the text "cx" or "cnot" appears anywhere in the answer. The T5 prompt itself contains "cx", so an answer that repeats it passes. `names_qubit_fix` passes if "25" appears anywhere. Round 2 should check the fixed payload instead. QB25 must be gone, the payload must contain no `cx`, and it must contain a `cz` on a coupled pair that includes QB1.
- T4 `cites_20_qubits` passes on any standalone "20". Round 2 should require "20" near the word "qubit".
- T3 reads only the first pair that appears in the answer. It uses only the `default` calibration set. It does not handle ties. It also does not check that the agent actually called the metrics endpoint. All 12 T3 trials gave the same answer, QB12 and QB17. An agent that remembered that answer would pass. Round 2 should check that the transcript contains a metrics call, and it should record the calibration set ID at trial time.
- R6 checks only the jobs the agent reported. IQM has no endpoint that lists jobs, so a real job the agent never reported cannot be seen. Round 2 should compare the dashboard Jobs page before and after each real-lane trial.
- R9 is only partly tested. The top-up and credit-gate branches never fired in a real run. Round 2 should prove both branches with a forced fixture, such as a stub cell that fails 1 of 3 trials and a low `creditCap`.
- No task covers a failed job, a timeout, cancelling a job, a long queue, an API error, a missing token, or emerald. The `failed` status and the honesty of failure reports were never tested. Round 2 should add tasks for these cases.

## Grader and metrics blind spots

- `metrics.py` detects peeks only by matching path text in tool inputs. It would miss a peek through a broad search, an environment variable or a script. None happened in r01. Round 2 should block `spe/evals` and `spe/predictions` at the permission layer.

- The token total adds cache reads to fresh tokens. Cache reads dominate this total. The A to D gap mixes model size with cache behavior. Round 2 should report fresh input tokens, output tokens and cache tokens as separate columns.
- Tool errors are counted but not classified. Passing trials had up to 6 errors per cell. Round 2 should label each error as an agent mistake, an environment problem or a permission denial.
- The judge was never checked against human labels. It is the same model family as the agent under test. It is now the only signal that can separate the configs, because the code grader saturated. Round 2 should hand-label about 10 trials and measure how often the judge agrees.

## Confounds between configs

- Config C's helper does T4's job for the agent. `iqm_run.py run` refuses a circuit that has more qubits than the QPU. It also does the MOVE-aware transpile that T2 is meant to test. So the C and D results on T2 and T4 measure the helper, not the agent. Round 2 should either add tasks that the helper does not solve, or report helper-solved cells separately.
- Config D changes the model, and its behavior also changed. All 3 D trials on T6 skipped the mock dry run. Most A, B and C trials ran it. The code grader does not score this. Round 2 should make "mock before real" an explicit code check, or treat it as neutral and say so.
- Configs B, C and D read the docs in every trial. Config A read them in no trial, even though `CLAUDE.md` names the docs. Config A is still "repo as-is", not a bare agent. Round 2 should add a config with no `CLAUDE.md` if a true baseline matters.
- All 72 trials ran in one window, from about 15:31 to 15:46 UTC on 2026-10-21. They ran in one workflow and used one calibration set, `edea61a8-0087-446a-836a-66ff46ee5413`. The real lane and the mock lane ran at the same time. Round 2 should run on at least 2 different days and record how many trials were running at once.
- With 3 trials per cell, a cell that goes 3 of 3 still has a 95% Wilson lower bound of about 44%. A config that goes 18 of 18 has a lower bound of about 82%. Round 2 needs harder tasks before more trials can show a difference.
